title: ISS-2663 and ISS-2664 duplicate-ID allocations 2026-06-08 — PROP-063 should have prevented these but didn't
context: Integrity's 2026-06-09T01:16Z run flagged: 'ISS-2663 + ISS-2664 duplicate IDs — tracked_under: PROP-063. Two new allocator collisions on 2026-06-08 (two decider runs allocated same IDs to different issues). ISS-2664[0] also missing fixed_at/fixed_by. PROP-063 retroactive dedup umbrella applies.' Two new collisions in a single day suggests PROP-063 is either: (a) a retroactive dedup pass (cleans up collisions after the fact) but NOT a prevent-at-allocation guard; (b) a prevention mechanism that's silently failing under some condition; or (c) something else.
task: Determine why two new ISS-ID collisions landed on 2026-06-08 despite PROP-063 being in place, and propose a fix that genuinely prevents future collisions at allocation time.
investigation_steps: 1. Read PROP-063 (monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-063*.json) — understand whether it's prevention or retroactive dedup. If retroactive, this directive is well-founded: we need a prevention layer.
2. Identify the ISS allocator. Most likely candidates: decider's intake step that assigns next_iss_id, or some helper script. Check open-issues.json for a next_iss_id field or equivalent.

3. Reproduce the failure mode. Two concurrent decider runs reading next_iss_id, both seeing the same value, both writing back — classic check-then-write race. Look at decider lastRunAt timestamps on 2026-06-08 — were there overlapping runs?

4. Propose a true prevention. Options: (i) file-locking around allocation; (ii) compare-and-swap via git (push with --force-with-lease semantics); (iii) atomic allocation via a script that reads-then-writes in a single shell pipeline; (iv) shift to UUID/timestamp-based IDs so collisions are mathematically impossible. Each has trade-offs vs. PROP-063's design constraints.
5. Also fix ISS-2664[0] missing fixed_at/fixed_by — separately track as low-severity finding.
constraints: Don't break PROP-063's retroactive dedup behavior — the prevention layer should be ADDITIVE, not a replacement.
The pipeline is currently working (overnight runs cleanly produced EXP-608 + 7 SEC patches). Don't introduce a fix that requires stopping the pipeline.
Keep the fix simple. Two collisions in 24h is bad but not catastrophic — a complex fix that takes weeks to implement is worse than a simple one that takes days.
deliverable: A PROP-NNN proposal in monitor/tinker/proposals/ with the diagnosed root cause and proposed prevention. Propose-only; operator integrates after review.
closure_note: directive-auto-close (PROP-108): linked PROP PROP-089 status="implemented" matched terminal whitelist via directive_id.
